hash_algorithm: blake2b-256 (digest_size=32, unkeyed) over canonical MessagePack of the flat argument array
segment_pattern_note: Full-string match REQUIRED (Python: re.fullmatch, not re.match — $ matches before a trailing newline). namespace additionally MUST NOT be exactly 'ns' or 'nsapi' (reserved: the server parses those key prefixes). The reservation is namespace-only; operation has no reserved values. Neither segment may contain '..' (the pattern admits it; the server rejects '..' anywhere in a key). A lone '.' stays valid.
width_coverage_note: All *16 header boundaries (uint/int widths, str8->str16, bin8->bin16, fixarray->array16, fixmap->map16, including the root argument array) are pinned by vectors. The *32 tier (str32/bin32/array32/map32, >=64 KiB or >=65536 elements) is normative and implemented by both tools but untested-by-design: fixture blobs that size would bloat the file without exercising different logic (same length-prefix code path, wider field).
error_vectors_note: The 'error' field is a human-readable reason for maintainers. Conformance means the input MUST be rejected with an error; the message text is not normative.
reader_vectors_note: Inputs for an interop VALUE reader, as raw MessagePack. A reader MUST decode every reader_accept_vectors document without error: each is well-formed but not canonical (a padded width, unsorted keys, a float32, a non-string map key, an ext type). Where tagged JSON can carry it, 'value' is what the document decodes to. A reader MUST reject every reader_reject_vectors document.

tagged_json.note: Single-key objects with a $-prefixed key are typed input tags; all other JSON maps directly.
tagged_json.$float: decimal float literal (JSON numbers are always integers in this file). Error vectors use 'nan' (parses to NaN in Python and JS) and '1e999' (overflows to +Infinity in Python, JS, and Rust) — never 'inf', which JS parses to NaN. A JavaScript harness must wrap the parsed Number in a type of its own (tools/interop-crosscheck.mjs uses a Float class), so the SDK can tell an explicit float from a bare Number, which this file only ever uses for a safe integer: an integral $float must still reach the SDK as a float ('2.0' stays float64 in a value, and '18446744073709551616' is a float64 argument, where a bare Number that large must be rejected).
tagged_json.$int: decimal integer literal (for values beyond 2^53, unsafe in JS JSON.parse)

key_vectors.name: empty_args
key_vectors.description: Zero arguments: canonical encoding of the empty array

key_vectors.name: single_int
key_vectors.description: Issue #1 example: users:get_user with one integer argument

key_vectors.name: uint64_max
key_vectors.description: Largest interop integer (2^64-1), e.g. a snowflake ID

key_vectors.name: int64_min
key_vectors.description: Smallest interop integer (-2^63)

key_vectors.name: uint_width_ladder
key_vectors.description: Every unsigned width boundary: 127/128 (fixint/uint8), 255/256 (uint8/uint16), 65535/65536 (uint16/uint32), 4294967295/4294967296 (uint32/uint64)

key_vectors.name: unicode_string
key_vectors.description: UTF-8 string, no Unicode normalization applied

key_vectors.name: str_width_ladder
key_vectors.description: String header boundaries by UTF-8 byte length: 31 (fixstr) / 32 (str8) / 255 (str8) / 256 (str16)

key_vectors.name: bin_width_ladder
key_vectors.description: Binary header boundaries: 255 bytes (bin8) / 256 bytes (bin16)

key_vectors.name: array_width_boundary
key_vectors.description: Array header boundary: 15 elements (fixarray) / 16 elements (array16)

key_vectors.name: map_width_boundary
key_vectors.description: Map header boundary: 15 keys (fixmap) / 16 keys (map16); zero-padded keys keep the sort order obvious

key_vectors.name: root_array16
key_vectors.description: 16 arguments: the ROOT canonical argument array itself uses array16

key_vectors.name: bool_null
key_vectors.description: Booleans and null

key_vectors.name: float_fractional
key_vectors.description: Non-integral float stays float64

key_vectors.name: float_integral_collapse
key_vectors.description: Number canonicalization: 2.0 encodes as int 2 (must equal single_int_two)

key_vectors.name: single_int_two
key_vectors.description: Int 2 — must produce the same key as float_integral_collapse

key_vectors.name: negative_zero
key_vectors.description: -0.0 is integral, collapses to int 0

key_vectors.name: float_large_integral_out_of_range
key_vectors.description: Integral float 2^64 exceeds uint64 -> stays float64

key_vectors.name: map_key_sort_ascii
key_vectors.description: Map keys sorted by code point: 'A' (0x41) before 'a' (0x61) before 'b'

key_vectors.name: map_key_sort_supplementary
key_vectors.description: Code-point order trap: U+FF61 sorts before U+10000. JS UTF-16 code-unit sort gets this BACKWARDS (0xD800 < 0xFF61).

key_vectors.name: nested_map_recursive_sort
key_vectors.description: Sorting applies at every nesting level

key_vectors.name: set_int_sorted
key_vectors.description: Set {3,1,2} -> elements sorted by encoded bytes -> [1,2,3]

key_vectors.name: set_heterogeneous
key_vectors.description: Set {'b', 10, 'a'} -> byte order puts int 10 (0x0a) before strings

key_vectors.name: set_mixed_sign_order
key_vectors.description: Set {-5, 'a', 1.5}: encoded-byte order is 'a' (0xa1..), 1.5 (0xcb..), -5 (0xfb) — NOT numeric/type-grouped order. Kills 'sort naturally, ints first' implementations.

key_vectors.name: float_collapse_lower_bound
key_vectors.description: Inclusive lower collapse bound: float -2^63 MUST collapse to the int64-min encoding (0xd3...), symmetric with the exclusive upper bound vector

key_vectors.name: set_dedupe_canonicalization
key_vectors.description: Set {2, 2.0}: number canonicalization makes the encodings identical; dedupe by encoded bytes leaves a single int 2

key_vectors.name: datetime_fractional
key_vectors.description: tz-aware datetime -> floor to micros -> one float64 division by 10^6

key_vectors.name: datetime_whole_second
key_vectors.description: Whole-second datetime yields integral float64 -> collapses to int

key_vectors.name: datetime_non_utc_offset
key_vectors.description: Non-UTC offset converts to the same instant (+05:30); key must equal datetime_fractional

key_vectors.name: datetime_pre_epoch
key_vectors.description: Pre-epoch datetime: negative timestamp (-0.876544), microseconds floored toward negative infinity

key_vectors.name: uuid_lowercased
key_vectors.description: UUID normalizes to lowercase hyphenated string (input was uppercase)

key_vectors.name: bytes_bin
key_vectors.description: Bytes encode as msgpack bin (never str family)

key_vectors.name: issue_example_mixed
key_vectors.description: Issue #1 vector: (42, 'hello', {'b': 2, 'a': 1})

key_vectors.name: reservation_scope
key_vectors.description: The ns/nsapi reservation is exact-match and namespace-only: namespace 'nsapix' (rejected by an ns* or nsapi* prefix match) and operation 'nsapi' stay valid

key_vectors.name: lone_dots_stay_valid
key_vectors.description: Only '..' is forbidden: a lone trailing '.' (namespace 'app.') and non-adjacent dots (operation 'users.fetch.by_id') stay valid

key_vectors.name: segment_max_length
key_vectors.description: Both segments at the 64-character limit (the longest interop key, 194 characters). The namespace starts with a digit and holds '-' and '_'; the operation starts with a digit and holds '.', '-' and '_'. A limit of 63, or a ban on a leading digit or on '-', rejects it

key_vectors.name: map_key_sort_case_across_letters
key_vectors.description: Code point order puts 'B' (0x42) before 'a' (0x61). A collator (Intl.Collator, localeCompare, with or without caseFirst 'upper') compares letters first and puts 'a' before 'B'

key_vectors.name: map_key_sort_punctuation
key_vectors.description: Code point order puts 'a-b' ('-' is 0x2d) before 'a_b' ('_' is 0x5f). A collator puts 'a_b' first: Unicode collation orders '_' before '-'

key_vectors.name: map_key_sort_shorter_key_later
key_vectors.description: Code point order puts 'ab' before the shorter 'b'. A length-first sort (shorter keys first, as canonical CBOR orders them, or by the encoded key with its header) puts 'b' first

key_vectors.name: map_key_sort_supplementary_shorter
key_vectors.description: Code point order puts U+FF61 U+FF61 (6 UTF-8 bytes) before the shorter U+10000 (4 bytes). A length-first sort and a UTF-16 code-unit sort both put U+10000 first

key_vectors.name: map_key_proto
key_vectors.description: '__proto__' is an ordinary string key. A JavaScript normalizer that copies keys by assignment (out[k] = v) sets the object's prototype instead, drops the key and mints the key of an empty map

key_vectors.name: set_in_map_normalized
key_vectors.description: A set inside a map value holding a tz-aware datetime and an uppercase UUID: each element is normalized before it is encoded and sorted (the int timestamp 0xce.. sorts before the str 0xd9..). The valid twin of reject_naive_datetime_nested, so a set path that rejects every datetime fails it

key_vectors.name: int_beyond_float64_precision
key_vectors.description: 2^53+1, -(2^53+1) and 2^63-1, then 2^53+1 again inside a list and a map value: integers inside int64 that a float64 cannot hold. A TypeScript SDK that turns a BigInt inside int64 into a Number rounds each one and mints a different key

key_vectors.name: small_int_as_bigint
key_vectors.description: Small integers passed as {"$int": ...} (a BigInt in JavaScript) take the shortest form, the bytes the same plain integers produce. An encoder that writes every BigInt at the full 9-byte width mints a different key

value_vectors.name: float_value_stays_float64
value_vectors.description: VALUE profile: no number canonicalization, 2.0 stays float64

value_vectors.name: datetime_sentinel_value
value_vectors.description: Temporal VALUES use the wire-format.md sentinel map convention

value_vectors.name: proto_key_value
value_vectors.description: A map whose key is '__proto__', an ordinary string key. A JavaScript reader or writer that sets keys by assignment changes the object's prototype instead and loses the entry

value_vectors.name: bom_strings_value
value_vectors.description: Strings that start with U+FEFF, one short and one of 300 characters: a reader keeps the character. A UTF-8 decoder left at its default (TextDecoder strips a leading BOM) drops it, and some MessagePack decoders use one only for longer strings

error_vectors.name: reject_nan
error_vectors.error: NaN is not allowed

error_vectors.name: reject_infinity
error_vectors.error: Infinity is not allowed (1e999 overflows to +inf in Python, JS, and Rust float parsers alike)

error_vectors.name: reject_negative_infinity
error_vectors.error: -Infinity is not allowed (independent vector: +Inf rejection does not imply -Inf rejection)

error_vectors.name: reject_int_overflow
error_vectors.error: integer above 2^64-1

error_vectors.name: reject_int_underflow
error_vectors.error: integer below -2^63

error_vectors.name: reject_naive_datetime
error_vectors.error: naive datetime (no UTC offset)

error_vectors.name: reject_uppercase_namespace
error_vectors.error: namespace must match the segment pattern

error_vectors.name: reject_colon_in_operation
error_vectors.error: operation must match the segment pattern

error_vectors.name: reject_trailing_newline
error_vectors.error: segment validation must be a FULL-string match (Python re.match + $ accepts a trailing newline; use fullmatch)

error_vectors.name: reject_reserved_namespace_ns
error_vectors.error: namespace 'ns' is reserved: the server parses a key starting 'ns:' as namespace-prefixed (here it would scope the key to a namespace named 'get_user')

error_vectors.name: reject_reserved_namespace_nsapi
error_vectors.error: namespace 'nsapi' is reserved: the server parses a key starting 'nsapi:' as namespace-prefixed (rejected whatever the operation, including one the server would 400 on for its '.')

error_vectors.name: reject_double_dot_namespace
error_vectors.error: namespace must not contain '..': the pattern admits it, but the server rejects '..' anywhere in a key

error_vectors.name: reject_double_dot_operation
error_vectors.error: operation must not contain '..': the pattern admits it, but the server rejects '..' anywhere in a key (here at the end of the segment, which a check that skips the last pair misses)

error_vectors.name: reject_namespace_too_long
error_vectors.error: namespace is 65 characters; the limit is 64 (segment_max_length pins 64 as valid)

error_vectors.name: reject_operation_too_long
error_vectors.error: operation is 65 characters; the limit is 64

error_vectors.name: reject_leading_dot_namespace
error_vectors.error: a segment must start with a letter or digit, not '.'

error_vectors.name: reject_leading_hyphen_operation
error_vectors.error: a segment must start with a letter or digit, not '-'

error_vectors.name: reject_leading_underscore_operation
error_vectors.error: a segment must start with a letter or digit, not '_' (a leading \w admits it)

error_vectors.name: reject_empty_namespace
error_vectors.error: a segment holds at least one character

error_vectors.name: reject_empty_operation
error_vectors.error: a segment holds at least one character

error_vectors.name: reject_non_ascii_digit_namespace
error_vectors.error: U+0663 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE is not an ASCII digit (Unicode \d, isdigit and isalnum admit it)

error_vectors.name: reject_non_ascii_letter_operation
error_vectors.error: U+00E9 is not an ASCII letter (a lowercase or alphanumeric test admits it)

error_vectors.name: reject_fullwidth_operation
error_vectors.error: full-width letters are not ASCII: NFKC folds them to 'get_user', and a segment is never normalized

error_vectors.name: reject_slash_namespace
error_vectors.error: '/' is not in the segment character set

error_vectors.name: reject_space_operation
error_vectors.error: a space is not in the segment character set

error_vectors.name: reject_uppercase_operation
error_vectors.error: operation must be lowercase

error_vectors.name: reject_colon_in_namespace
error_vectors.error: ':' is not in the segment character set (it would add a key segment)

error_vectors.name: reject_trailing_newline_operation
error_vectors.error: segment validation must be a FULL-string match, on the operation as on the namespace

error_vectors.name: reject_naive_datetime_nested
error_vectors.error: naive datetime inside a set inside a map value

error_vectors.name: reject_nan_nested
error_vectors.error: NaN inside a map value inside a list

error_vectors.name: reject_int_overflow_in_list
error_vectors.error: integer above 2^64-1 inside a list

error_vectors.name: reject_int_underflow_in_map
error_vectors.error: integer below -2^63 inside a map value

error_vectors.name: reject_int_overflow_in_map
error_vectors.error: integer above 2^64-1 inside a map value (with reject_int_underflow_in_list, each bound is pinned on both paths)

error_vectors.name: reject_int_underflow_in_list
error_vectors.error: integer below -2^63 inside a list

reader_accept_vectors.name: reader_padded_int_widths
reader_accept_vectors.description: Integers in wider forms than the shortest: 42 as uint16, -1 as int32, 1 as uint64

reader_accept_vectors.name: reader_padded_headers
reader_accept_vectors.description: Headers wider than needed: an array16 of 3 holding 'abc' as str8, {'a': 1} as map16 and 2 bytes as bin16

reader_accept_vectors.name: reader_unsorted_map_keys
reader_accept_vectors.description: Map keys in the reverse of code point order

reader_accept_vectors.name: reader_float32
reader_accept_vectors.description: 1.5 as a float32 (0xca), which canonical writers never emit

reader_accept_vectors.name: reader_non_string_map_key
reader_accept_vectors.description: {1: 42}: a map with an integer key. No tagged-JSON value can carry it; a reader must decode it without error (msgpack-python's unpackb needs strict_map_key=False)

reader_accept_vectors.name: reader_ext_type
reader_accept_vectors.description: An application ext type (fixext1, type 1, payload 0x2a). No tagged-JSON value can carry it; a reader must decode it without error

reader_reject_vectors.name: reader_trailing_byte
reader_reject_vectors.description: The issue_example_object value followed by one 0x00 byte: a complete document and a trailing byte, with no CK frame prefix, so only the general trailing-bytes check rejects it. A reader that strips trailing NUL padding before a strict decode accepts it, so it fails this vector too
reader_reject_vectors.error: trailing bytes after one complete document

aad_vectors.name: interop_key_aad
aad_vectors.description: AAD v0x03 over an interop key; format=msgpack, compressed=False (always, in interop mode)

encryption_vectors.name: interop_encryption_roundtrip
encryption_vectors.description: Full interop encryption round-trip: HKDF-SHA256 per spec/encryption.md (same master key + tenant as test-vectors/encryption.json, hence the same derived key), AES-256-GCM over the PLAIN MessagePack value bytes (no ByteStorage step) with the interop_key_aad AAD and a fixed nonce.
